stem: A 42-year-old man comes to the office due to several months of numbness and tingling in both legs and difficulty walking.  He has also noticed that he tires more easily with physical activity.  Temperature is 36.8 C (98.2 F), blood pressure is 122/86 mm Hg, pulse is 76 /min, and respirations are 14/min.  Physical examination shows conjunctival pallor and loss of vibration and position sensation in the bilateral lower extremities with associated gait ataxia.  The remainder of the examination is within normal limits.  Which of the following findings is most likely to be present upon further questioning of the patient?​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​​​​​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌

options.label: D

explanation:
This patient likely has vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency.  Vitamin B12 is obtained by eating fortified foods (eg, breakfast cereal) or animal products (eg, meat, dairy, eggs).  Because it is not present in plants, strict vegans are at risk for dietary deficiency.  Enteral absorption of vitamin B12 is largely dependent on intrinsic factor (IF), a glycoprotein produced by parietal cells of the stomach.  Therefore, vitamin B12 deficiency also occurs in the setting of parietal cell loss (eg, gastrectomy) or damage (eg, pernicious anemia, gastritis).

Vitamin B12 deficiency typically takes years to manifest because hepatic stores are massive and can last around 1-2 thousand days.  Patients with vitamin B12 deficiency typically develop one or both of the following:

  • Megaloblastic anemia:  Vitamin B12 is required for purine and pyrimidine synthesis; therefore, deficiency impairs DNA replication.  Cells with rapid turnover (eg, hematologic, gastrointestinal) are primarily affected.  Hematologic changes include macrocytosis and hypersegmented neutrophils as well as anemia (eg, pale conjunctiva).

  • Subacute combined degeneration:  Impaired myelin synthesis impairs neuronal conduction, particularly in the dorsal and lateral columns.  Manifestations typically include symmetric neuropathy (eg, paresthesia, weakness), loss of vibration/position sensation, and an ataxic gait.  The longer the deficiency is untreated, the less likely the neurologic deficits can be reversed.

(Choice A)  Isoniazid competes with vitamin B6 in the production of neurotransmitters, which can result in peripheral neuropathy in high-risk patients (eg, pregnancy, HIV, diabetes mellitus).  Although severe vitamin B6 deficiency can cause anemia, it is rare for isoniazid therapy to outcompete vitamin B6 to a degree that causes anemia.

(Choice C)  Gastrectomy can cause B12 deficiency, but it usually takes years (not 8 months) to manifest due to the large hepatic stores.  Although vitamin E deficiency can cause hemolysis and neurologic symptoms, patients with gastrectomy rarely develop this deficiency.

(Choice D)  Phenytoin, an antiepileptic drug used to treat focal and generalized seizures, may cause folate deficiency, leading to megaloblastic anemia.  Phenytoin can also cause peripheral neuropathy, but this adverse effect usually occurs only with chronic therapy (>1 year).

(Choice E)  Vitamin D deficiency can develop due to inadequate dietary intake and minimal sunlight exposure.  This deficiency presents as rickets in children and osteomalacia or osteoporosis in adults.

Educational objective:Vitamin B12 is obtained through a diet that includes fortified foods and animal sources.  Strict vegans are at risk for dietary deficiency.  Manifestations include megaloblastic anemia and potentially irreversible neurologic deficits (eg, paresthesia, weakness, ataxic gait).​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​​​​​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌
